title: Marguerite and the Debt
premise: Silas Yarrow, a burned-out private security contractor, is approached by a woman named Marguerite who claims he saved her life years ago in Lagos—a debt she intends to repay. But Silas remembers no such rescue, and as Marguerite's 'interest' payments begin arriving—money, information, protection—he realizes the fabricated favor is a leash: someone powerful wants him indebted, compliant, and positioned inside the security firm guarding a whistleblower named Ada Okonkwo. When Silas discovers Marguerite engineered his entire reputation to place him exactly where she needs him, he must choose between destroying the evidence that could exonerate him from the incident that ruined his sleep and his career, or handing it to Ada and burning every bridge—including the one back to his own survival. In the end, Silas gives up the secret, accepts arrest, and finds the first real night's sleep he's had in years.
about_author: Sable Oyelaran is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients whose names she still can't say aloud. She writes thrillers about people who discover their pasts were never really theirs to begin with.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Silas Yarrow, running on four hours of broken sleep, works a routine protection detail for a nervous tech executive. A woman named Marguerite intercepts him afterward, thanking him for saving her life in Lagos seven years ago. He has no memory of it. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in his carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: An envelope arrives containing cash, a burner phone, and a photograph of Silas at the Lagos hotel he does vaguely remember—dated the night of the incident. Marguerite calls: the debt isn't money; it's access. She wants an introduction to his firm's newest client file. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Silas's boss, Renata Voss, briefs the team on their new principal: Ada Okonkwo, a former auditor threatening to expose the Meridian Group's laundering network. Silas recognizes Meridian's name from Marguerite's paperwork. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the trap's outline becomes visible, and he walks into it anyway.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter in Marguerite's POV: her recruitment by Meridian fixer Callum Reeve, her years as an asset, and the moment she was ordered to manufacture a savior for Silas Yarrow. We learn she chose this assignment—or claims she did. Emotional beat: cold competence masking something unresolved.

chapters.title: The Incident
chapters.summary: Silas relives the Lagos night in fragments: gunfire in a stairwell, a colleague named Tomas bleeding out, and the report Silas signed that contradicted what he saw. The official version kept him employed; the truth would have ended him. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: guilt as a physical weight.

chapters.title: First Payment
chapters.summary: Marguerite delivers her first 'gift': proof that someone inside Voss's firm is feeding Meridian details of Ada's schedule. She frames it as loyalty to Silas. He can't tell if she's protecting him or testing how fast he reports to her. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: paranoia metastasizing.

chapters.title: Ada Okonkwo Sleeps Fine
chapters.summary: On protective detail, Silas observes Ada—calm, methodical, unafraid in a way he envies. She notices him noticing and asks blunt questions about his insomnia. Their first real conversation. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: reluctant admiration, the first warmth in the book.

chapters.title: Callum Reeve
chapters.summary: Meridian's fixer makes contact, all charm and implied violence, making clear that Marguerite's debts are Meridian's debts—and so are Silas's now. He offers Silas a clean exit in exchange for Ada's travel itinerary. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the walls closing in, temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Silas traces the leak to Dev, a colleague and the closest thing he has to a friend. Confronting him privately, Silas learns Dev is drowning in gambling debt and terrified. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling—exposing Dev protects Ada but destroys a man already breaking.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV again: she meets Reeve, plays the loyal asset, and secretly copies files on Silas's manufactured history. A hint surfaces that her Lagos story contains one true detail she's never told anyone—not even Reeve. Emotional beat: the reader begins to suspect her motives are not Meridian's.

chapters.title: The Safehouse
chapters.summary: After a tail is spotted, Ada is moved to a safehouse Silas designed. Alone with her overnight, he almost tells her about the incident and the debt. Instead she tells him why she's doing this: her brother died cleaning up Meridian's books. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: intimacy forged under siege.

chapters.title: Collateral
chapters.summary: Reeve escalates: Dev is found dead, staged as a suicide, hours after Silas decided not to turn him in. The message is unmistakable—hesitation costs lives, and Silas's hesitation specifically. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into rage.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Owes
chapters.summary: Marguerite breaks cover partially, showing Silas the ledger of everything Meridian made her do—including fabricating his heroism. She claims the favor was a lie built around one true thing: she was in that stairwell in Lagos, and she pulled the trigger that killed Tomas. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the ground giving way entirely.

chapters.title: The Report
chapters.summary: Silas digs up his original draft incident report—the one he rewrote—hidden in an old encrypted drive. It names the man who actually ordered the stairwell ambush: a Meridian director. This document is the secret worth killing for. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Two Buyers
chapters.summary: Reeve offers Silas immunity and a new identity for the report. Ada, unknowing, asks Silas directly whether anything about him isn't what it seems. Marguerite warns him both buyers intend to burn the document and everyone near it. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cornered from every direction at once.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Silas tells Ada everything: the rewritten report, the debt, Marguerite, Dev. She doesn't forgive him—she recalculates. Together they plan to move the report to journalists before Meridian can act, using Silas's own security protocols against his employers. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: relief and fear arriving together.

chapters.title: The Extraction That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Meridian moves early, hitting the safehouse. Silas gets Ada out through routes only he knew, but Marguerite is captured covering their escape—whether deliberately or not, even she may not know. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: adrenaline, then hollow panic.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Reeve offers a final trade: Marguerite's life for the original report, delivered in person, alone. Silas understands no version of this ends cleanly. He copies the report three ways and prepares for the meeting knowing at least two of them are lies. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grim resolve.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: At a disused freight terminal, Silas faces Reeve and a captive Marguerite. He hands over a drive; Reeve's men verify it as authentic. As Reeve orders both killed anyway, police sirens—Ada's contingency—flood the terminal. Reeve escapes; Marguerite doesn't. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: climax—victory and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, the report reaches journalists; Meridian's directors fall in slow motion across the news cycle. Silas learns Marguerite had mailed him a letter before the exchange, held by a lawyer, timed to arrive after. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's letter reveals the whole truth: she didn't kill Tomas—she took the blame for Reeve, and inventing Silas's debt was her only way to put someone inside Meridian's next operation. Her final line: 'You were never the debtor. I just needed you to believe you were.' POV: Silas reading. Emotional beat: devastating reframe of the entire book.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Silas testifies, loses his license, and expects to feel ruined. Instead, in a small apartment with no clients and no secrets left, he sleeps through the night for the first time since Lagos. The price of survival, paid in full, turns out to be survivable. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution.
